result.topic_en: Conjectural statements about 'Mersenne's primes' (exponents p for which 2^p-1 is prime), classifying them by whether they can be written as a^2+ab+b^2 or a^2+b^2, and giving theorems for generating such primes.

When $2^p-1$ is a prime, $p$ may be termed as a Mersenne's Prime
(1.) All Mersenne's primes are either of the form $a^2+ab+b^2$ or of the form $a^2+b^2$. Then since a number of the form $12n-1$ cannot be expressed in any one of the above two forms, we infer that
(2) A Mersenne's prime is never of the form $12n-1$. Thus for example $2^{11}-1$, $2^{23}-1$, $2^{47}-1$, $2^{59}-1$, $2^{71}-1$, $2^{83}-1$, $2^{107}-1$, $2^{131}-1$, $2^{167}-1$, $2^{179}-1$, $2^{191}-1$, $2^{227}-1$, $2^{239}-1$, $2^{251}-1$, &c should be composite numbers. Hence we may divide all Mersenne's primes into two classes, one comprising primes that can be expressed as $a^2+ab+b^2$ and the other containing primes that cannot be expressed as $a^2+ab+b^2$.
(3) Hence the Mersenne's primes of the 1st class except 1 and 3 are of the form $6n+1$, while those of the 2nd except 2 are of the form $12n+5$. Thus we have,

items.quote: All Mersenne's primes are either of the form $a^2+ab+b^2$ or of the form $a^2+b^2$.
items.english: Every exponent p with 2^p-1 prime is of the form a^2+ab+b^2 or a^2+b^2.

items.quote: A Mersenne's prime is never of the form $12n-1$.
items.english: No such exponent is congruent to -1 mod 12.
These Mersenne numbers should be composite.

items.quote: If $P$ be any prime, and $p$ any odd prime and if either of $\frac{P^p-1}{P-1}$ or $\frac{P^p-1}{p(P-1)}$ happens to be a prime, then that prime will be a Mersenne's prime of the 1st class.
items.english: For any prime P and odd prime p, if (P^p-1)/(P-1) or (P^p-1)/(p(P-1)) is prime, then 2 raised to it minus 1 is prime and it is of first class.

items.quote: If $P$ be any prime and if either of $P^2+P+1$ or $\frac{P^2+P+1}{3}$ happens to be a prime, then that prime will be a Mersenne's prime of the 1st class.
items.english: For any prime P, if P^2+P+1 or (P^2+P+1)/3 is prime, it is a first-class Mersenne exponent.

items.quote: If $p$ be a Mersenne's prime, then $2^p-1$ will be a Mersenne's prime of the 1st class..
items.english: If 2^p-1 is prime, then 2^(2^p-1)-1 is also prime, and 2^p-1 is of the first class.
